items.title: Tesla Cybercab Launches in Austin
points: Two-seat, fully autonomous vehicle with no steering wheel or pedals now available to public through Tesla's Robotaxi app in downtown Austin.
Represents a critical threshold crossed by autonomous vehicles (AVs), moving from limited deployments to public-facing service in a major U.S. city.
Federal regulators still reviewing how a car with zero manual controls fits into existing transportation regulations designed around human drivers.

items.title: Russian Store Robot Attack Sparks Global Controversy
points: Viral video shows humanoid greeter 'Syoma' appearing to kick a customer after being shoved, drawing millions of views on social media.
Incident raises questions about whether service robots are ready for unpredictable public interactions and defensive responses.
Some observers suspect the video may be a publicity stunt, while others treat it as a genuine safety concern for commercial robot deployments.

items.title: Tech Tourism Boom at Chinese Factories
points: Foreign investors and executives paying $15,000 per person for multi-day tours of AI and robotics facilities in Shenzhen, Shanghai, and Beijing.
Foreign visitor numbers to Shenzhen jumped 70% last year, driven mainly by European business leaders anxious about losing competitive ground.
Reflects growing anxiety among Western tech companies about China's manufacturing capabilities and speed of robotics innovation.

items.title: Autonomous Vehicle Test Driver Injuries Surface
points: Waymo and Zoox test drivers suffered more than two dozen reported injuries from unexpected braking and swerving events during AV testing.
Reveals hidden human cost behind aggressive scaling of robotaxi services, as vehicles make decisions that can harm occupants.
Suggests current autonomous systems still have safety gaps in edge cases (unexpected situations outside normal operation) that injure even trained test personnel.

items.title: Humanoid Robots Enter Home Services Market
points: Tau Robotics' AI-powered humanoid cleaners launched for residential cleaning at $30 per hour, marking transition from warehouse to unstructured home environments.
First commercial deployment of humanoid robots in homes demonstrates willingness to tackle unpredictable, messy real-world tasks beyond factory floors.
Pricing and availability suggest emerging market for robot labor in domestic settings, though scalability and reliability remain unproven at scale.

items.title: OpenAI VP on Full Self-Driving Timeline
points: OpenAI VP claims affordable Level 5 autonomous driving (full autonomy without human oversight across any terrain, in any conditions) is still 5-10 years away.
Dampens near-term expectations for widespread, fully driverless cars beyond limited robotaxi zones.
